topic: IFA weekly fee paid by councils (England)
figure: Average of £820 per week
context: The CMA's final-report England summary (10 March 2022) says fostering prices paid by local authorities have been steady at an average of £820 per week, based on data for the largest independent fostering agencies in 2016-2020.
quote: In fostering, prices have been steady at an average of £820 per week.

source.title: Children's social care market study: final report, England summary (para 23)

topic: IFA weekly fee paid by councils (England) - CMA interim figures for 2020
figure: About £820 per week (2020, largest providers), with 19% average operating profit margin
context: The CMA press release on its interim report gives 2020 figures for the largest providers: fostering agencies charged about £820 per week with a 19% operating margin, versus £3,830 per week and 23% for children's homes.
quote: for fostering agencies, the average weekly price for fostering was about £820 per week, with an average operating profit margin of 19%

source.title: CMA outlines concerns on availability and price of children's care (press release)

topic: IFA average annual fee per child (largest providers)
figure: Average fee per child of £42,626 per year, flat from FY2016 to FY2020
context: CMA financial analysis of the eight large fostering providers found the average annual fee per child was flat at £42,626 across FY2016-2020; it also found local authority operating costs were approximately 36.8% lower than those of the large private providers.
quote: the average fee per child has remained flat from FY 2016 to 2020 at an average of £42,626.

source.title: Children's social care market study: interim report, Appendix A: Financial analysis (para 83)

topic: IFA operating profit margins
figure: Average operating profit margin of 19.4% for the largest IFAs
context: The CMA final-report England summary says profit margins of the largest independent fostering agencies appear consistently high; its Appendix A gives the same 19.4% as the FY2016-2020 average for the eight large fostering providers (19.8% for PE-owned, 17.8% for non-PE-owned).
quote: profit margins of the largest IFAs appear consistently high at an average of 19.4%.

source.title: Children's social care market study: final report, England summary (para 23)

topic: IFA operating profit margins - DfE restatement (2026)
figure: 19.4% average operating margin for largest IFAs vs 10.3% net rate of return for private non-financial corporations in 2024
context: The DfE's February 2026 fostering strategy repeats the CMA margin figure and contrasts it with the economy-wide corporate rate of return; the same document says IFAs now provide 45% of mainstream fostering households and 48% of filled places.
quote: the largest IFAs make average operating margins of 19.4%. This is much higher than the annual net rate of return for private non-financial corporations, which was 10.3% in 2024.

source.title: Renewing Fostering: homes for 10,000 more children (CP 1503), p.14

topic: IFA vs in-house weekly placement cost (sector source, secondary)
figure: Average in-house (LA) placement £440 per week vs average IFA placement approximately £800 per week
context: The Fostering Network's September 2025 consultation response cites a 2023 source (Perryman, 2023) for these averages; the figures are secondary and not from an official dataset.
quote: The average in-house (LA) placement costs £440 per week ... the average IFA placement costs approximately £800 per week

source.title: Modernising and improving the administration of council tax consultation: The Fostering Network's response (p.2)

topic: Cost of assessing one foster carer applicant (sector source, uncited)
figure: Assessment costs of £10,000 to £15,000 per candidate
context: FosterWiki, a foster-carer-led organisation, states this range in its 2025 impact report with no citation, footnote or link for the figure; no official (DfE, Ofsted, CoramBAAF, Fostering Network or council) cost-per-approval figure could be confirmed in this research.
quote: With assessment costs ranging from £10,000 to £15,000 per candidate, the loss of 7 out of 10 applicants represents a considerable waste of public resources

source.title: 2025 Recruitment and Retention Impact Report

topic: Cost of a regional recruitment hub relative to approvals (break-even)
figure: Hub would have needed to recruit 88 approved fostering households in year one to break even; DfE invested £3.4 million in 2023/24 in the pathfinder hub
context: Ipsos UK and CEI's DfE-commissioned interim evaluation of the Foster with North East pathfinder hub used a break-even approach comparing hub costs (to August 2024) against projected placement savings.
quote: the Hub would have needed to recruit 88 approved foster care households in the first year of operation.

source.title: Evaluation of Foster with North East: Interim report (RR 1555), Executive Summary, Economic analysis
source.publisher: Department for Education (Ipsos UK and Centre for Evidence and Implementation)

topic: Enquiry-to-application conversion rate (national, DfE/Ipsos)
figure: 6% of enquiries progressed to application (year ending 31 March 2022)
context: DfE-commissioned Ipsos research on foster carer recruitment and conversion rates reports that only 6% of initial enquiries at fostering services progressed to the application stage; the same report notes enquiries were 18% higher than in the year ending 31 March 2018.
quote: In the year ending 31 March 2022, 6% of enquiries at fostering services progressed to the application stage.

source.title: Foster carer recruitment and conversion rates: Research report (Chapter 1, p.9)

topic: Enquiries vs newly approved carers (national, 2024-25)
figure: Almost 150,000 enquiries but only 7,365 newly approved foster carers in 2024-25; 6% of enquiries progressed to application in year ending 31 March 2025
context: The DfE's February 2026 fostering strategy gives the latest national enquiry-to-approval picture (carers are individuals, not households).
quote: In 2024–25 there were almost 150,000 enquiries but only 7,365 newly approved foster carers.

source.title: Renewing Fostering: homes for 10,000 more children (CP 1503), p.15 and p.31

topic: Enquiries, applications and application approval rate (national, 2020-21)
figure: 160,635 initial enquiries; 10,145 (6%) applications; 32% of applications approved (vs 44% in 2015-16); enquiry-to-application rate down from 12% in 2014-15
context: House of Commons Library debate pack summarising Ofsted fostering statistics for the year ending 31 March 2021.
quote: There were 160,635 initial enquiries from prospective fostering households in the year ending 31 March 2021 ... only 10,145 (6%) foster carer applications were received.

source.title: General debate on the recruitment and retention of foster carers (Debate Pack CDP-2022-0080)

topic: Enquiry-to-approval conversion by sector, 2021-22 (Ofsted data analysed by CEI)
figure: Local authorities: 31,045 enquiries, 3,665 applications, 675 approved (2.17% of enquiries); IFAs: 4,615 applications, 900 approved (0.84% of enquiries)
context: CEI's research report for The Fostering Network analysed Ofsted's 2021-22 fostering data; approvals here are applications completed in approval within the year, so the rates understate eventual approvals.
quote: local authorities only received 3,665 applications which led to just 675 approved applications (2.17% of the original enquiries made)

source.title: Foster carer retention and recruitment in England: A research report for The Fostering Network (Section 2.1, pp.10-11)
source.publisher: Centre for Evidence and Implementation / The Fostering Network

topic: Enquiry-to-approval conversion (council example, East Sussex)
figure: Enquiry-to-approval conversion rate of 11% in 2023-24 (236 enquiries, 26 approvals); 7%-9% in the four prior years
context: East Sussex County Council's fostering annual report table shows enquiry to initial visit at 19% and initial visit to approval at 58% in 2023-24.
quote: Conversion rate: Enquiry to approval ... 8% | 9% | 7% | 9% | 11% (2019-20 to 2023-24)

source.title: East Sussex Fostering Services Annual Progress Report 2023/24 (Appendix 1)

topic: Enquiry-to-approval conversion (council example, Barnet)
figure: 279 enquiries in 2024/25 (138 from Facebook lead-generation ads); conversion rate rose from 2.1% (2023/24) to 5.73% (2024/25); 12 mainstream/respite/supported lodgings carers approved
context: London Borough of Barnet's Fostering Service Annual Report 2024/25 gives a full enquiry-journey table for the year.
quote: During 2024/25, 279 enquiries were received, in comparison to 241 in 2023/24 and 174 in 2022/23.

source.title: The Fostering Service Annual Report 2024/25 (Appendix B)

topic: Enquiry-to-application conversion (regional hub vs national)
figure: Foster with North East hub: 23.1% of enquiries progressed to successful application vs a national rate of 12%; more than 850 enquiries in first year
context: Sunderland City Council news item marking the first birthday of the DfE-funded Foster with North East pathfinder hub.
quote: is also much higher at 23.1 per cent than the national rate of 12 per cent

source.title: Trailblazing fostering hub celebrates its first birthday

topic: Marketing spend on carer recruitment (regional hub communications campaign)
figure: £300,000 total investment in the hub's October 2023-March 2024 communications campaign, including £100,000 for media buying; a further £200,000 allocated for 2024/25
context: The only published marketing-spend figure found; it relates to the DfE-funded Foster with North East pathfinder hub campaign, not to an individual agency. No credible published figure for typical Google Ads costs for fostering keywords was found.
quote: with a total investment of £300,000, including £100,000 allocated directly to the Hub for media buying.

source.title: Evaluation of Foster with North East: Interim report (RR 1555), Chapter 4, Communications campaign
source.publisher: Department for Education (Ipsos UK and Centre for Evidence and Implementation)

topic: Share of enquiries from digital marketing (council example)
figure: Digital marketing responsible for 80% of enquiries; enquiries rose from 509 (2024/25) to 677 (2025/26) with 17 approvals in 2025/26
context: Shropshire Council's March 2026 fostering briefing; useful as evidence that councils depend heavily on digital channels for enquiries.
quote: this digital marketing is responsible for 80% of our enquiries

source.title: Fostering Briefing Update, March 2026 (Item 7, Appendix 2)

topic: Ofsted fostering statistics 2024-25: fostering households
figure: 42,190 fostering households at 31 March 2025 (down 1% on the year and 7% since 2021); 18,415 mainstream LA households and 15,020 mainstream IFA households; IFAs 45% of mainstream households
context: Ofsted's annual fostering in England statistics for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025, published 26 November 2025.
quote: At the end of March 2025, there were 42,190 fostering households in England.

source.title: Main findings: fostering in England 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025

topic: Ofsted fostering statistics 2024-25: approved foster carers and places
figure: 56,345 approved mainstream foster carers (down 1% from 57,065; down 12% from 63,890 in 2021); 69,825 approved mainstream places (down from 70,465); around 60% of places filled
context: Ofsted's annual fostering in England statistics for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025.
quote: As at March 2025, there were 56,345 approved mainstream foster carers.

source.title: Main findings: fostering in England 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025

topic: Ofsted fostering statistics 2024-25: applications
figure: 8,290 applications received in 2024-25 (down from 8,485 in 2023-24); 2,050 applications completed in approval during the year
context: Ofsted's annual fostering in England statistics for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025; initial enquiries are not reported in this publication.
quote: The number of applications received during the period 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 was 8,290.

source.title: Main findings: fostering in England 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025

topic: Ofsted fostering statistics 2024-25: approvals and deregistrations
figure: 4,430 mainstream households joined the sector (3,050 new to fostering); 4,115 newly approved households at end March 2025; 4,690 deregistrations (12% of the 38,125 households at the start of the year)
context: Ofsted's annual fostering in England statistics for 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025 show deregistrations again exceeding new approvals.
quote: During this period, 4,430 mainstream households joined the sector, of which 3,050 were new to fostering. ... The number of deregistrations over the same period was 4,690.

source.title: Main findings: fostering in England 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025

topic: Ofsted fostering statistics 2023-24 (prior year, for trend)
figure: 42,615 fostering households (vs 45,370 in 2021); 4,055 households approved; 4,820 stopped fostering; net loss of 765 households
context: The Fostering Network's summary of Ofsted's 2023-24 statistics, the third successive annual fall in foster carer numbers.
quote: A total of 4,055 fostering households were approved during the year ... 4,820 stopped fostering

source.title: New Ofsted data shows number of foster carers in England declining for third year running
